q: Section 7.14 forbids an architect from appropriating or unfairly taking advantage of another architect's ideas unless which condition is met?
o: A signed non-compete agreement
Express permission from the architect who originated the idea
Payment of a licensing fee to the UAP
Prior publication of the idea in a journal
n: Section 7.14 bars appropriating the intellectual property or unduly taking advantage of another architect's ideas without express authority from the originating architect. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.14)

q: An architect wants press coverage of a finished project. Which action would violate Section 3.5?
o: Letting the publication photograph the finished project
Answering interview questions about the design process
Giving the magazine straightforward project facts
Soliciting ads or financial support to help cover the cost of a feature about his/her own work
n: Section 3.5 prohibits soliciting (or permitting solicitation of) advertisements or support for the cost of a publication presenting the architect's own work, and bars paid endorsement advertising of construction materials/equipment. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.5)

q: Per Section 11's effectivity clause, under what condition does the Code become effective?
o: Fifteen (15) days after full publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation
Immediately once the Board Chairman signs it
On the first day of the next calendar year
Thirty (30) days after Senate ratification
n: Section 11 provides the Resolution takes effect after fifteen (15) days following its full and complete publication in the Official Gazette or any daily newspaper of general circulation in the Philippines. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VIII, Sec. 11)

q: Section 7.8 says an architect should avoid lending his/her name to, or associating with, what type of enterprise?
o: One not accredited by IAPOA, even if otherwise legitimate
One based outside the Philippines
One that could damage the architect's standing or the profession's reputation
A direct business competitor
n: Section 7.8 requires refraining from association with, or allowing use of one's name by, any enterprise that may negatively affect the architect or the architectural profession. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.8)

q: According to the resolution's attestation clause, where and when was the Code of Ethical Conduct executed?
o: Cebu City, April 15, 2006
Manila, April 5, 2006
Quezon City, April 5, 2004
Manila, January 2, 2006
n: The resolution's closing attestation states it was done in the City of Manila, this 5th day of April, 2006. (Source: Board of Architecture Resolution No. 02, s. 2006, Attestation)

q: Taken together, what do Sections 4.11 and 4.12 require of the architect regarding project timing and client communication?
o: Reporting to the client only when the project is finished
Handing all client communication to the contractor
Working without needless delay within an agreed time frame, and keeping the client updated on progress and anything affecting cost or quality
Finishing every project within a flat 30-day period
n: Section 4.11 requires work without undue delay within an agreed reasonable time limit; Section 4.12 requires keeping the Client informed at all times of progress and of any issue affecting quality or cost. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Secs. 4.11-4.12)

q: What does Section 7.13 require regarding an architect's internal office arrangements?
o: A single-person office setup exclusively
Handing all quality control over to the client
Sound and effective internal systems, including review procedures and enough qualified, properly supervised staff
An open-door approach with no formal procedures
n: Section 7.13 requires the architect's practice to have appropriate and effective internal procedures, including monitoring and review processes, and sufficient qualified and supervised staff to function efficiently. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.13)

q: Section 9 states violators are liable under specified provisions of R.A. No. 9266 together with Board Resolution No. 07, s. 2004. Which R.A. 9266 provisions are cited?
o: Sec. 2, Art. I and Sec. 5, Art. II
Sec. 23(f), Art. III and Sec. 29, Art. IV
Sec. 7(g), Art. II and Sec. 14, Art. I
Sec. 30, Art. V and Sec. 31, Art. V
n: Section 9 cites liability under Sec. 23(f), Art. III and Sec. 29, Art. IV of R.A. No. 9266, and the corresponding Sec. 23(f), Rule III and Sec. 29, Rule IV of Board Resolution No. 07, Series of 2004. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VIII, Sec. 9)

q: An independent consultant is informally asked to quote a fee before any official engagement exists. What does Section 7.16 direct?
o: Quote the highest allowable rate as a safeguard
Refuse to ever discuss fees informally
Give a low quote right away to win the client over
Withhold a fee quote until formally invited to give one, and first gather enough project information to prepare a sound proposal
n: Section 7.16 requires not quoting a fee without first receiving an official invitation, and having sufficient project information to prepare a clear fee proposal, protecting the Client and public from under-resourcing or underpricing. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.16)

q: Once the architect personally observes and inspects material, equipment, or workmanship that does not conform, what does Section 5.3 require?
o: Leaving it in place unless the client objects
Prompt rejection or condemnation, to prevent needless delay and extra expense to the Contractor
Referring it to an outside engineer before doing anything
Holding off until the project is finished
n: Section 5.3 requires immediate rejection or condemnation, upon personal knowledge and inspection, of material/equipment/workmanship not conforming to the Contract Documents, precisely to avoid unnecessary delay and additional expense. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. IV, Sec. 5.3)

q: Under Section 3.6, what must support an architect's claim to a professional specialization?
o: A self-professed preference for that area
Academic credentials, a relevant track record, adequate professional resources, and recognition from peers
One finished project of that type
The client's approval alone
n: Section 3.6 bars deceiving the public as to competence; a specialization claim must be supported by academic qualification, track record of relevant expertise, adequate professional resources, and sanction by peers in the profession. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.6)

q: If a court declares one section of the Code unconstitutional, what does Section 10's separability clause say happens to the rest?
o: The whole Code is automatically nullified
Only Article I stays in effect
The unaffected sections remain valid and unimpaired
The UAP must re-ratify the entire Code
n: Section 10 provides that a declaration of unconstitutionality or invalidity of any section/part shall not affect, invalidate, or impair the other sections or provisions not directly involved in that judgment. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VIII, Sec. 10)

q: A project looks financially or legally unworkable. Per Section 4.3, what must the architect do, even if it costs the commission?
o: Say nothing and leave the client to find out later
Advise the client not to move forward with the project
Proceed anyway to keep the fee
Hand the client off to another architect without explanation
n: Section 4.3 requires the architect to advise a Client against proceeding with a project of questionable practicability due to financial or legal conditions, even if it means losing the commission. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.3)

q: Who signed as Chairman of the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture on the Code of Ethical Conduct resolution?
o: Miguel R. Caluza
Carlos G. Almelor
Eugene G. Gan
Leonor Tripon-Rosero
n: The resolution was signed by Eugene G. Gan as Chairman, with Fernando L. Santos and Miguel R. Caluza as Members, attested to by Secretary Carlos G. Almelor, and approved by PRC Chairperson Leonor Tripon-Rosero. (Source: Board of Architecture Resolution No. 02, s. 2006, Signatories)

q: An architect has a personal stake in a materials supply business that touches a current client's project. What does Section 4.9 require?
o: Keeping it quiet since it's a personal matter
Transferring the stake to a relative rather than disclosing it
Informing the client of the situation
Doing nothing unless the client finds out on their own
n: Section 4.9 requires the architect to remain free from financial/personal interests that could weaken his/her impartiality, and to inform the Client if any other business interest would relate to or affect the Client's interest. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.9)

q: A project is already committed to another architect, though negotiations remain pending. What does Section 7.4 forbid?
o: Simply asking about the project's status
Referring the client to a third architect
Soliciting that project by any means whatsoever
Discussing the project casually at a professional gathering
n: Section 7.4 prohibits soliciting, by any means, a project already known to be previously committed to another architect, whether that commitment is still under negotiation or already definitely agreed. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.4)

q: Which Board of Architecture issuance adopted the Code of Ethical Conduct for registered and licensed architects?
o: Resolution No. 01, Series of 2006
Resolution No. 07, Series of 2004
Resolution No. 02, Series of 2006
Resolution No. 03, Series of 2004
n: The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture adopted and promulgated the Code through Resolution No. 02, Series of 2006. (Source: Board of Architecture Resolution No. 02, Series of 2006)

q: Regarding compensation, what must the written commission agreement state under Section 7.17.4?
o: The client's overall project budget only
The architect's personal tax bracket
The contractor's markup percentage
The fee itself, or the formula for calculating it
n: Section 7.17.4 requires the written agreement to specify the fee or the method of calculating it. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.17.4)

q: Section 5.2 bars the architect from knowingly doing what with oversights or errors found in the Contract Documents?
o: Disclosing them to the client at all
Documenting them in the project file
Correcting them at his/her own expense
Making the Contractor fix them to the financial detriment of the Contractor or Owner
n: Section 5.2 bars the architect from knowingly calling upon the Contractor to remedy oversights or errors in the Contract Documents to the Contractor's or Owner's financial disadvantage. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. IV, Sec. 5.2)

q: What must an architect give the Contractor, per Section 5.1, to prevent avoidable mistakes and added costs?
o: A copy of his/her own fee schedule
Access to the client's financial records
Clear, definite, and consistent contract-document information
Only verbal instructions during site visits
n: Section 5.1 requires giving the Contractor every reasonable assistance by furnishing clear, definite, and consistent information on the contract documents. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. IV, Sec. 5.1)

q: Section 6.2 bars seeking commissions, discounts, gifts, or favors from material suppliers/agents, and requires any market discount obtained be handled how?
o: Kept by the architect as extra pay
Split evenly with the contractor
Credited to the client
Donated to the IAPOA
n: Section 6.2 bars seeking such commissions/discounts/gifts that would place the architect in a reciprocal frame of mind, and requires all market discounts be credited to the Client. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. V, Sec. 6.2)

q: Which R.A. No. 9266 provision gave the Board authority to adopt the Code of Ethical Conduct?
o: Section 14, Article I
Section 29, Article IV
Section 7(g), Article II
Section 23(f), Article III
n: The Board resolved to adopt and promulgate the Code pursuant to Section 7(g), Article II of R.A. No. 9266. (Source: R.A. No. 9266, Sec. 7(g), Art. II)

q: At the court's discretion, Section 9 sets a fine for Code violations within what range?
o: A flat Php1,000,000 with no range
n: Section 9 provides for a fine of not less than One hundred thousand pesos (Php100,000.00) but not more than Five million pesos (Php5,000,000.00), in addition to or apart from suspension/revocation/cancellation and imprisonment. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VIII, Sec. 9)

q: Section 7.22 bars discrimination on which grounds, provided they don't impair professional performance?
o: Membership in a competing organization
Race, national origin, age, gender, marital status, religion, or disability
Years of experience alone
Choice of design software
n: Section 7.22 prohibits discrimination on grounds of race, national origin, age, gender, marital status, religion, or any disability that would not hinder the person's professional work performance. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.22)

q: An architect served as Professional Adviser who helped draft a design competition's program. Under Section 7.3, can that architect later join as a contestant?
o: Yes, provided a different firm files the entry
Yes, if he/she tells the organizers about the earlier role
No — anyone who helped formulate the program, or served as Adviser or Juror, is barred from competing
Yes, if the competition rules don't address it
n: Section 7.3 bars an architect from entering as a competitor in any competition where he/she had direct involvement in formulating the program, or was engaged as Professional Adviser or Juror; similarly, an adviser/juror cannot later be retained as an Architect for that project except as Consulting Architect. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.3)

q: When must the architect determine, with the client, the scope of services and the fees involved, per Section 4.2?
o: Only after design development wraps up
Only if the client raises the question
At the very start of the business relationship
Only at the final billing stage
n: Section 4.2 requires the architect to acquaint/ascertain the scope of services and inform the client of corresponding fees at the very inception of their business relationship. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.2)

q: Besides a suitable work environment and fair pay, what else does Section 7.10 require of an employer-architect toward staff?
o: Covering only their board-exam review costs
Guaranteed lifetime employment
Requiring NDAs before any mentoring
Helping their career growth, and mentoring young aspirants in ethical practice
n: Section 7.10 requires providing a suitable work environment, fair compensation, and facilitation of professional advancement, plus tutoring and mentoring young aspirants toward the ideals and ethical practice of the profession. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.10)

q: Section 7.15 says an architect's reputation should rest on what basis, while recognizing whose contributions?
o: Seniority alone, regardless of ongoing competence
Advertising volume rather than work quality
Comparisons that downplay competitors
The quality of his/her own service, while crediting others for work they performed
n: Section 7.15 requires building reputation on the merits of one's own service and performance, continuously updating professional know-how, and recognizing/crediting others for professional work performed. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.15)

q: What does Section 7.7 forbid an architect from doing toward a colleague?
o: Citing a colleague's published work with proper credit
Offering constructive peer feedback at a professional forum
Unfairly or maliciously criticizing or discrediting another architect or his/her work
Publishing an objective comparative study
n: Section 7.7 simply prohibits maliciously or unfairly criticizing or discrediting another Architect or that architect's work. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.7)

q: Beyond a fine, what imprisonment term and administrative sanctions can Section 9 impose for a violation?
o: A flat 30-day jail term only
A mandatory life term with no other sanction
Six (6) months to six (6) years imprisonment, and/or suspension or revocation of the certificate of registration, or cancellation of the special/temporary permit
Community service instead of any other penalty
n: Section 9 provides that violators shall be meted suspension or revocation of the certificate of registration, or cancellation of the special/temporary permit, and/or a fine, or imprisonment of not less than six (6) months nor exceeding six (6) years, or both, at the court's discretion. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VIII, Sec. 9)

q: According to Section 5's opening statement, what does the Contractor rely on the Architect to do?
o: Protect only the client's interests
Guarantee the contractor the highest possible profit
Represent the contractor in disputes against the client
Fairly protect the contractor's interests along with the client's
n: Section 5's chapeau states the Contractor depends upon the Architect to safeguard fairly the Contractor's interests as well as those of the Client. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. IV, Sec. 5)

q: A project sits within a community with historic districts and natural heritage. What must the architect do under Section 3.1?
o: Skip the site entirely if heritage features exist
Respect and help preserve the community's heritage and value system while improving the environment sustainably
Defer entirely to the local zoning board
Favor the client's aesthetic wishes over heritage concerns
n: Section 3.1 obliges the architect to respect and help conserve the community's values and heritage, and to improve the environment and habitat sustainably, mindful of the widest interests of users. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.1)

q: An architect-employee is leaving the firm. Can he/she take project designs or data along, per Section 7.21?
o: Only with the client's, never the employer's, permission
Freely, since he/she did the work personally
Not without the employer's consent, which the employer must not unreasonably withhold except to protect legitimate confidentiality
Only after reimbursing the firm for materials
n: Section 7.21 bars a departing architect-employee from taking designs, drawings, data, or other relevant materials without the employer's permission, even if personally performed, while requiring the employer not to unreasonably withhold such permission except where confidentiality must be protected. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.21)

q: Which body, acting as the IAPOA, issued the Code of Ethical Conduct?
o: The Professional Regulation Commission directly
The Association of Structural Engineers of the Philippines
United Architects of the Philippines, Inc. (UAP)
The Philippine Institute of Architects
n: The Code was prescribed and issued by the United Architects of the Philippines, Inc. (UAP), the IAPOA, by virtue of Board Resolution No. 03, Series of 2004, as approved by the Commission. (Source: Board Resolution No. 02, s. 2006, Preamble; Board Res. No. 03, s. 2004)

q: What is the official title of R.A. No. 9266, under which the Code was issued?
o: The Engineering Practice Act
The Professional Regulation Act
The Architecture Act of 2004
The Building Code of the Philippines
n: R.A. No. 9266 is known as “The Architecture Act of 2004.” (Source: R.A. No. 9266, Title)

q: What must the client agreement include regarding disputes, per Section 4.10?
o: A waiver of the client's right to dispute billing
A clause naming the architect sole arbiter of disputes
A clause requiring court litigation for every dispute
A clause for negotiation, mediation/conciliation, and/or arbitration as alternative dispute-resolution methods
n: Section 4.10 requires including in the Client agreement a clause for negotiation, mediation/conciliation, and/or arbitration as alternative dispute resolution methods. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.10)

q: What do Sections 7.18 and 7.19 together call on the architect to advance?
o: Financial management skills alone
Marketing and public relations alone
Aesthetic excellence, functional logic, education, research, training, and practice, plus the allied arts and construction-industry knowledge
Building code compliance alone
n: Section 7.18 requires continuously raising standards of aesthetic excellence, functional logic, architectural education, research, training, and practice; Section 7.19 requires promoting the allied arts and contributing to construction industry knowledge and capability. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Secs. 7.18-7.19)

q: Per Section 1, the architecture profession calls for people with what combination of qualities?
o: Strict legal and litigation skill
Only artistic talent and creativity
Purely technical and engineering competence
The highest responsiveness, business acumen, sensibility, and both artistic and technical ability
n: Section 1 states the profession calls for men and women of the highest responsiveness, business acumen, sensibility, as well as artistic and technical ability. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. I, Sec. 1)

q: May an architect build the very project for which he/she prepared the plans, under Section 4.7?
o: No, this is always a conflict of interest
Only if the client waives the right to complain
Only on government-funded projects
Yes, so long as it follows the relevant Standards of Professional Practice provisions
n: Section 4.7 permits an architect to undertake construction of a project he/she designed, so long as it conforms with the pertinent sections of the Standards of Professional Practice. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.7)

q: Section 7.17 lists six items the written commission agreement must cover. Which of these is NOT one of them?
o: Scope of work
The architect's personal educational background
Any termination provision
The chosen mode of alternative dispute resolution
n: Section 7.17 lists six required written terms: scope of work (7.17.1), delineation of responsibilities (7.17.2), any limitation of responsibilities (7.17.3), fee or method of calculating it (7.17.4), mode of alternative dispute resolution (7.17.5), and any provision for termination (7.17.6). The architect's personal educational background is not one of them. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.17 (7.17.1-7.17.6))

q: After promptly inspecting each finished phase found compliant, what must the architect issue under Section 5.5?
o: A notarized affidavit of good workmanship
The relevant Certificates of Payment, and eventually the final Certificate of Completion
Verbal approval only, undocumented
A revised set of plans
n: Section 5.5 requires the architect to promptly inspect each completed phase and, if conforming, issue the corresponding Certificates of Payment and, respectively, the final Certificate of Completion. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. IV, Sec. 5.5)

q: Though barred from paid ads and self-promotion, what may an architect do under Section 3.4 and even be paid for it?
o: Offer referral cash incentives to clients
Pay for billboard ads of the firm
Write books, act as a columnist, or join seminars/forums that advance public understanding of the profession
Hire a publicist to inflate the portfolio
n: Section 3.4 allows an architect to write books, be a regular columnist, contribute literature, or participate in forums/seminars/workshops to advance public knowledge, and to receive remuneration or honorarium for such undertakings. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.4)

q: Which kind of offer from a Contractor or Sub-contractor must the architect turn down under Section 5.4?
o: Standard progress reports
Legitimate invoices for completed work
Requests for design clarification
Free engineering/design services, or substantial gifts/commissions that create a reciprocal obligation
n: Section 5.4 requires rejecting offers of free professional engineering/allied design services, or substantial aid, gifts, commissions, or favors from a Contractor/Sub-contractor that would place the architect under an obligation to reciprocate. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. IV, Sec. 5.4)

q: Section 6.1 forbids soliciting free professional or technical services from a manufacturer/supplier when doing so would do what?
o: Merely require crediting the supplier in documents
Require the supplier to give product samples
Create an obligation harmful to the client's interest, or affect the architect's professional judgment
Reduce the client's overall budget
n: Section 6.1 prohibits soliciting such free services when accompanied by an obligation detrimental to the Client's best interest, or one that may adversely affect the architect's professional opinion. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. V, Sec. 6.1)

q: An architect is hired to add onto a heritage building designed by someone else. What must he/she do under Section 7.6?
o: Take full authorship credit for the whole structure
Proceed silently since the owner changed
Demolish the original heritage elements to simplify the design
Notify the original architect, limit authorship claims to the new work if the original design still predominates, and weigh restoration given the heritage value
n: Section 7.6 requires notifying the original architect even where the Client/Owner has changed, limiting the new architect's claim of authorship to the specific added work when the original design predominates, and considering restoration possibilities for structures involving architectural heritage. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.6)

q: What do Sections 7.11 and 7.12 together require toward colleagues, young aspirants, and the profession?
o: Billing colleagues for technical advice
Limiting IAPOA involvement to paying dues
Sharing knowledge and experience unselfishly, fostering unity, and giving time to the profession's advancement through active IAPOA involvement
Withholding proprietary methods from competitors
n: Section 7.11 requires unselfishly sharing technical knowledge/experience with colleagues and young aspirants and fostering unity; Section 7.12 requires unselfishly giving time and effort to the profession's advancement through active, personal commitment to the IAPOA. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Secs. 7.11-7.12)

q: Donating professional services to gain a competitive edge is barred under Section 7.2, except for what kind of project?
o: Any government project regardless of scale
Family projects
Worthy civic or religious undertakings
Any project where a rival already gave a discount
n: Section 7.2 requires abiding by the Basic Minimum Fee and bars using donated services for competitive advantage, except for worthy civic or religious projects; competitive sketch submissions are also restricted to the Architectural Competition Code framework. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.2)

q: Section 4.6 says fees billed should match the architect's work, standing, and experience, anchored to what standard?
o: The contractor's cost estimate alone
A freely negotiated fee with no benchmark
The Basic Minimum Fee under the Standards of Professional Practice
Government-assessed property value
n: Section 4.6 ties professional fee billing to the Basic Minimum Fee prescribed under the “Standards of Professional Practice.” (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.6)

q: In the Architect's Credo, whose interest is placed above the architect's own when asking for fair pay?
o: The architect's own firm
The contractor's
The client's
The government's
n: The Credo states: “I shall ask for fair remuneration for my professional services from my Client, and hold his/her interest over and above my own.” (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VII, Sec. 8 (Credo))

q: Under Section 4.4, can an architect guarantee a cost estimate to land a commission?
o: Yes, always, to reassure the client
Only for residential work
No, except where the law itself provides for it, as in some government projects
No guarantee is ever allowed, period
n: Section 4.4 requires explaining the conditional character of estimates; the architect shall not guarantee estimates or cost of work to secure a commission, unless provided for by law (e.g., in certain government projects). (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.4)

q: The Architect's Credo pledges to disclose, when required, what kind of personal matter that might create a conflict of interest?
o: Religious affiliation
Private business investments or ventures
Personal medical history
Relationships with subordinates
n: The Credo states: “I shall disclose, whenever required, any private business investments or ventures that may tend to create a conflict of interest...” (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VII, Sec. 8 (Credo))

q: Section 7's introduction describes moral responsibilities toward which three groups?
o: Family, competitors, and regulators only
Foreign architects, banks, and insurers
His/her profession, colleagues, and subordinates
Contractors, suppliers, and building inspectors
n: Section 7 states the Architect has moral responsibilities towards his/her profession, colleagues, and subordinates. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7)

q: The Credo's closing line pledges the highest professionalism, integrity, and competence toward which groups?
o: Only fellow UAP members
Only future architecture students
The public, client, contractor, manufacturers/dealers/agents, and colleagues/subordinates
Only the client and the architect's family
n: The Credo's closing pledge consecrates the architect to the highest standard of professionalism, integrity, and competence to the public, the Client, the contractor, the manufacturers, dealers, and agents, and to colleagues and subordinates as the direct and indirect users/beneficiaries of the architect's services. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VII, Sec. 8 (Credo))

q: Section 2 charges the architect with impartial mediation/conciliation between which two parties?
o: Client and sub-contractor's suppliers
Client and Contractor
UAP and PRC
Government and Contractor
n: Section 2 charges the Architect with mediation/conciliation functions between the Client and the Contractor, requiring entire impartiality. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. I, Sec. 2)

q: A prospective client wants free preliminary sketches before signing anything, for a shot at the job. What does Section 4.1 require?
o: Bill only for materials, treating design labor as free
Provide the sketches for free since it's common practice
Decline — introducing services must be limited to prior work examples, without free preliminary sketches absent a compensation agreement
Provide free sketches only for repeat clients
n: Section 4.1 limits an architect's introduction of services to presenting examples of prior experience, and prohibits offering free preliminary sketches or other services without a compensation agreement. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.1)

q: As good citizenship under Section 3.3, an architect must do all of the following EXCEPT which one?
o: Comply with the Code and the Standards of Professional Practice
Act to advance his/her own interest even at the profession's expense
Observe government laws and regulations
Properly follow laws on architectural practice and building design/planning
n: Section 3.3 explicitly says the architect shall at no time act in a manner detrimental to the best interest of the architectural profession — the opposite of choice d. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.3)

q: Every page of the PRBoA resolution identifies the Code by what document title?
o: SPP Document 301: Code of Conduct
IAPOA Document 001
UAP Document 200: Code of Ethical Conduct
UAP Document 100: Standards of Professional Practice
n: Each page of the promulgated Code is footed “UAP Document 200 : Code of Ethical Conduct.” (Source: UAP Document 200)

q: Besides registered and licensed architects, the Code also governs holders of what other authorization?
o: Provisional UAP membership
Apprenticeship certificates
Foreign reciprocity licenses
Temporary/special permits issued under R.A. No. 9266
n: The Code applies to registered and licensed architects and to holders of temporary/special permits issued under R.A. No. 9266. (Source: Board Resolution No. 02, s. 2006, Title/Preamble)

q: When is a registered architect expected to recite the Architect's Credo, per Section 8?
o: Only once, at initial registration
Only at Board disciplinary hearings
On special occasions such as mass oath-taking, IAPOA affairs, or PRBOA events
Every time a project contract is signed
n: Section 8 requires every registered and licensed architect to recite the Architect's Credo with vigor, passion, and hope during special or important occasions such as mass oath-taking, IAPOA affairs, or PRBOA events. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VII, Sec. 8)

q: Section 4 grounds the Architect-Client relationship on what principle, never sacrificing what higher interest?
o: Mutual profit maximization; the architect's reputation
Confidentiality alone; the contractor's finances
Strict written contract only; client convenience above all
Good faith; never at the expense of the public interest and welfare
n: Section 4 provides the Architect-Client relationship is dependent upon good faith, and the Architect must always protect the Client's interests but never at the expense of higher public interests and welfare. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4)

q: How does Section 6's chapeau characterize the exchange of technical information between architects and material suppliers/manufacturers?
o: Limited strictly to written correspondence
Permitted only via the UAP national office
Prohibited outright
Necessary, and so encouraged and commended, subject to conditions
n: Section 6 describes such exchange as necessary and therefore encouraged and commended, subject to the conditions in 6.1 and 6.2. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. V, Sec. 6)

q: A junior draftsman finishes a full plan set with no supervision from the principal architect. Can that architect sign and seal the plans, per Section 7.9?
o: Yes, as long as it gets a quick review before submission
Yes, since the draftsman is in the same firm
No — an architect must not affix signature and seal to work not done under his/her direct personal supervision
Yes, if the client agrees
n: Section 7.9 prohibits an architect from affixing signature and seal to any plans or professional documents not prepared under his/her direct personal supervision. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.9)

q: A prospective client wants preliminary design work started “just to see” before signing a contract. What does Section 7.1 direct?
o: Proceed informally since no fee has been discussed
Have a junior staffer do it unofficially
Decline — services, including preliminary ones, must not be rendered or conditionally offered without a professional service agreement
Proceed but bill only if a contract later gets signed
n: Section 7.1 prohibits rendering professional services without a professional service agreement, and bars offering or providing preliminary services on a conditional basis prior to a definite agreement. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.1)

q: Under Section 4.8, where must an architect's compensation come from exclusively?
o: Manufacturer commissions
Contractor referral fees
A mix of client fees and supplier kickbacks
The professional fee billed directly to the client, with no return from any other source
n: Section 4.8 requires the architect be compensated solely by the professional fee billed directly to the Client, and bars asking for any other returns from any other source. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.8)

q: Under Section 3.2, what civic duty does the architect owe toward his/her professional organization?
o: Avoid contact with other design professions
Just pay dues on time
Promote its interests and help advance its objectives and services
Withhold technical info from the construction industry
n: Section 3.2 requires the architect to promote the interest of the professional organization and share in the interchange of technical information with other professions and the construction industry. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.2)

q: Section 4.5 requires balancing the client's needs and budget against what wider concern?
o: The general contractor's preferences alone
Competing firms' profitability
The effects of the work on the public and community's life and well-being
The architect's own marketing needs
n: Section 4.5 requires the architect to consider the Client's needs and budget together with the effects of the work on the public and community, aiming to meet aesthetic and functional requirements commensurate with the budget. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.5)

q: How may an architect display a professional shingle or project billboard, per Section 3.7?
o: Not at all — any display counts as self-advertising
Only inside the office, never on-site
Outside the office or at the site, done modestly, possibly with pictures
Only with a competing architect's written approval
n: Section 3.7 permits exhibiting a professional shingle outside the office, or a project billboard with relevant information (possibly including pictures), provided it is done in a modest manner. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.7)

q: An architect reasonably believes, based on solid information, that a colleague violated the Code. What must he/she do under Section 7.20?
o: Confront the colleague privately and drop it
Post about it on social media
File a formal complaint with the designated body
Ignore it unless a client is directly harmed
n: Section 7.20 obliges an architect possessing substantial information supporting a reasonable belief of a Code violation by another architect to file a formal complaint with the designated body. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.20)

q: Beyond the client, Section 2 extends the architect's duties to which other parties?
o: Only government regulators
Professional associates, subordinates, and the public
Only competing architects
Only future occupants of the building
n: Section 2 provides the Architect has moral responsibilities to professional associates and subordinates, and is engaged in a profession carrying grave responsibilities to the public. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. I, Sec. 2)

q: A client wants a new architect, but the prior one was never formally let go. What must the new architect do first, per Section 7.5?
o: Proceed since the client may switch architects freely
Have the client sign a liability waiver
Wait for the previous architect to complain first
Notify the previous architect in writing and confirm the earlier engagement was ended and fully paid
n: Section 7.5 requires notifying the previously employed Architect in writing and conclusively determining that the original employment has been terminated and duly compensated for, before undertaking the commission. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.5)
